item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm tomorrow
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm tomorrow. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm tomorrow.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm tomorrow on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Sigatoka father travels to parliament to call for tougher criminal justice laws after son's death
item.description: A grieving father who travelled from Sigatoka with his family to call for changes to Fiji's criminal justice system says victims and their families need greater protection, while serious offenders must face stronger consequences. While speaking to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights, Sachida Nand of Kulukulu, Sigatoka, is calling for a comprehensive review of Fiji
item.content:encoded:
A grieving father who travelled from Sigatoka with his family to call for changes to Fiji's criminal justice system says victims and their families need greater protection, while serious offenders must face stronger consequences.

While speaking to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights, Sachida Nand of Kulukulu, Sigatoka, is calling for a comprehensive review of Fiji's bail, sentencing, parole and repeat-offender laws following the death of his son after an alleged assault.

Nand and his sons were allegedly assaulted last month following a confrontation over an incident involving one of his farm animals.

His son later died as a result of the alleged assault and was laid to rest at Koromumu Cemetery.

Ratu Vula Maimuri Ratuva and his son Ratu Kinijoji Ranovo Ratuva have been charged for the assault and murder of 38-year-old Vimal Vikash Nand.

Meanwhile, on behalf of the Speaker and whole of Parliament, Committee Chairman Ratu Rakuita Vakalalabure conveyed their condolences and says they will take his submissions into consideration.

Ratu Rakuita advised Nand that the committee will not interfere with the case, as his late son’s case is currently before the court.

Among Nand's proposals is the establishment of a compensation system or fund to provide financial assistance to families of victims of serious crimes.

Nand is also calling for Fiji's bail laws to be reviewed, particularly for people charged with serious violent offences.

He says bail should not be automatic in serious cases and that courts should give greater consideration to factors including flight risk, interference with witnesses, intimidation of victims, the possibility of re-offending and the danger posed to the wider community.

He has proposed stronger bail conditions, including regular reporting to Police, the surrender of travel documents, restrictions on movement and prohibitions on contacting victims or witnesses.

Nand is also urging Parliament to consider electronic monitoring, including ankle bracelets, for accused people released on bail who are identified as presenting a risk.

On sentencing, Nand is calling for serious violent offences to attract severe and proportionate penalties and says Parliament should consider substantial minimum non-parole periods for appropriate serious offences.

Nand says laws dealing with repeat offenders should also be strengthened and that the criminal justice system must provide an effective deterrent against serious violent offending.

However, Nand says reforms must continue to respect the rights of accused persons, including the presumption of innocence, due process, judicial independence and the right to a fair trial.

He is calling for a comprehensive review of Fiji's criminal justice laws involving judges, prosecutors, defence lawyers, Police, Corrections authorities, victim-support organisations, criminologists and members of the wider community.

Nand says the review should identify legislative gaps, including inadequate penalties, weak supervision mechanisms and inconsistencies in sentencing, and address these through evidence-based law reform.

He says the objective should not simply be to impose harsher punishments, but to create a criminal justice system that is credible, consistent, transparent and effective in protecting society.

Nand says his submissions are driven by the experience of his family and the need to prevent other families from enduring a similar tragedy.

item.title: Paddlers take 500km journey around Viti Levu to protect Fiji's living waters
item.description: Pacific Conference of Churches General Secretary Reverend James Bhagwan says every community they visit will be more than just another stop on the map where the team will stop in coastal communities to listen to people whose livelihoods, culture and daily lives depend on rivers, mangroves, reefs, coastlines and the ocean. He says the paddlers will listen and learn about the environmental challenge
item.content:encoded:
Pacific Conference of Churches General Secretary Reverend James Bhagwan says every community they visit will be more than just another stop on the map where the team will stop in coastal communities to listen to people whose livelihoods, culture and daily lives depend on rivers, mangroves, reefs, coastlines and the ocean.

He says the paddlers will listen and learn about the environmental challenges communities are facing, and highlght the local knowledge and solutions already being used to respond to them .

Reverend Bhagwan adds the journey is one where communities, churches and young people will take part in coastal clean-ups, waste sorting, recycling awareness, environmental education, prayer, worship and talanoa.

He says the ocean is part of Fiji's home and is a source of food, identity, spirituality and life however, it continues to be affected by plastic pollution, unsustainable consumption and the growing impacts of climate change.

Meanwhile, Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme Director of Waste Management and Pollution Control Anthony Talouli says poorly managed waste on land can travel through drains, rivers and other waterways before eventually reaching the ocean.

He says this threatens marine ecosystems, people's livelihoods and the wellbeing of communities.

Talouli says protecting the ocean therefore begins with choices made in homes, communities and businesses.

He says the journey will also provide an avenue for community voices to feed into Fiji and the Pacific's priorities ahead of PreCOP31 and COP31.

Talouli says these priorities include keeping the 1.5-degree global warming limit within reach, improving access to climate finance, strengthening recognition of the relationship between the ocean and climate, and ensuring Pacific voices and leadership are heard internationally.

Permanent Secretary for Environment and Climate Change Dr Sivendra Michael says meaningful environmental action starts at the local level, but these efforts must also connect with national, regional and global action on climate change, ocean degradation and plastic pollution.

He says everyone has a responsibility to protect Fiji's living waters for future generations.

The team paddled from the National Sailing Centre to Suva Foreshore and Muaivuso on Tiesday before paddling Togoru and Navukavu in Navua yesterday where they discussed about plastic waste with the Vanua and church and had a training session run by the Waste Recyclers Fiji.

They paddled to Rovadrau, the Pearl Resort and Lomary today.

The team is calling for stronger protection and restoration of rivers, mangroves, reefs and coastal ecosystems, reductions in plastic production and pollution, stronger community recycling initiatives, greater support for locally led climate adaptation and resilience and for frontline communities to have a meaningful role in decisions affecting their land, water and future.

The initiative is organised by the Pacific Conference of Churches and Suva SUPers as part of the 2026 Season of Creation under the theme "Living Waters and supported by the Australian Government through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, SPREP through its Pacific Ocean Litter Project, and Fiji's Ministry of Environment and Climate Change.

item.title: Uciwai residents demand urgent action over deteriorating road
item.description: A long-running road problem in Uciwai, Nadi, has reached a critical point, with residents saying years of complaints have gone unanswered while dust and potholes continue to affect their health, businesses and daily lives. Uciwai resident Selema Wati Evans says residents have been raising concerns about the condition of the road for years, but little has been done to address the problem permanentl
item.content:encoded:
A long-running road problem in Uciwai, Nadi, has reached a critical point, with residents saying years of complaints have gone unanswered while dust and potholes continue to affect their health, businesses and daily lives.

Uciwai resident Selema Wati Evans says residents have been raising concerns about the condition of the road for years, but little has been done to address the problem permanently.

Evans says she began raising the issue after purchasing land in the area several years ago and continued to follow up after moving there with her husband and family.

She says the wider Uciwai community had already been complaining about the road for years before her family moved there.

Evans says she recently lodged another complaint with the Fiji Roads Authority and followed the required process by collecting signatures from residents through a petition.

She says she has also received letters of support from community representatives and businesses in the area, highlighting the ongoing concerns over the road.

Evans says the deteriorating condition is particularly concerning for people living close to the roadside, especially school students, because of the amount of dust generated by passing vehicles.

Insert: Selema - Businesses affected Sept 03

Evans says Uciwai advisory councillor Mahendra Reddy has also raised concerns about the road and its impact on the community and businesses.

According to Evans, previous work on the road has not provided a lasting solution.

She says potholes have been patched or sections of the road worked on, but residents want the road properly repaired rather than receiving temporary fixes.

Evans is calling for urgent action, saying residents should not have to continue living with the same road conditions after years of complaints.

Questions have been sent to the Fiji Roads Authority. We are awaiting their response.
